about: What real use, and the person Pit Board is for, showed must change or must stay true in Windstorm Pit Board, and the version each is due in. A lesson here is a gate, not a note: tests/test_g21_promises.py (G21.14) refuses a version while a row due in it is not built, and refuses the version after it until the row says where it was proven on a real machine.
how_to_use: A new lesson gets a row the day it is learned: what was seen, the promise, a codon in DNA-STRAND-MASTER-PLAN.md, the version it is due in, and a tracking issue when work is left.
When it is built: put the name of its test in 'test'. The test must exist under tests/ and be named with the row's codon (test_G10_5_... for G10.5).
When it has been seen to work on a real machine: say which machine, which version and when in 'proven'.

'ship_in' moves only with a reason in 'moved_why'. A row whose owner is 'person' was seen by the person Pit Board is for, on their own machine: its date moves only by their word, restated in 'moved_by_person'.
A row is never deleted. A promise that turns out wrong is closed by a row that says why.
A lesson that was heard and not taken goes under 'declined' with the reason, so that nothing is dropped without a word.

rows.seen: 2026-11-21, the M1 pilot, on the operator's own machine: the operator asked where the pilot was running, because they saw no red dot. The status segment was there, at the end of line 11 of an 11-line status line, after the operator's own fields.
rows.promise: Pit Board's status segment is printed first: before a one-line status line, joined with ' · ', or on its own first line above a status line of several lines, so a long status line never hides it.

rows.seen: 2026-11-22, a reboot of the machine the pilot runs on: the lane log was byte-identical before and after, the open ask kept its ID, uid and state, the board listed the same asks, and the start-up reminder and the status segment worked with nothing re-armed. Only things outside Pit Board were lost (the session's temporary files and its own scheduled checks).
rows.promise: A reboot loses no ask and leaves Pit Board nothing to re-arm: asks live only in the lane logs on disk (INV2), and the hooks and the status line wrapper are files that run on each call.
rows.proven: The pilot machine, 0.1.0 (the pilot copy), 2026-11-22T04:19Z: reads of the lane log, the asks and the board before the reboot and after it matched.

rows.seen: 2026-11-22, the same reboot: the terminal tab showing the pilot lane got a new id and kept its label. The tmux pane id saved with an ask before the reboot (%148) no longer existed; the lane came back as %10, because a new tmux server gives pane ids out again from the start. Its window name changed too (bash to claude).
rows.promise: Waking (G16.5) types into a saved pane only when it still runs Claude Code, its tmux session name equals the ask's where.tmux_session and its folder equals where.cwd; never by a saved id alone, and window names are not compared.

rows.seen: The M1 pilot, 2026-11-17 to 2026-11-22: the agent recorded its one real ask to the operator unprompted (A2, 2026-11-21 Eastern), so acceptance item 2 was shown on 1 of its 2 days. A second day could not come, because the pilot lane's decisions go to its owner, not to the operator; a made-up ask would be a false proof. The skill's owner ruled on 2026-11-22 that item 2 moves to M2a.
rows.promise: The agent records its asks to the operator with pitboard add without being reminded, on two days.
rows.proof_needed: Two calendar days, each with at least one real ask recorded unprompted in an M2a lane; name the dates and the lanes.

rows.seen: 2026-11-22, the first night Pit Board was installed in single lanes' folders on two test machines (a shared Linux laptop and an Intel Mac): a machine with no Pit Board home could get one from pitboard setup --minimal --apply only together with a change to the user's own statusLine setting, which reaches every session of that user. The folder installer had to make the home itself, without that step.
rows.promise: pitboard setup has a folder mode: it makes the Pit Board home and sets the status line wrapper in one folder's .claude/settings.local.json, never in the user's settings, and its undo puts that file back byte for byte (or removes only Pit Board's entries if the file changed since).

rows.seen: 2026-11-22, the same night, on the Intel Mac: pgrep -x claude sees a Claude Code session's process name as its version file (2.1.330), so counting the sessions in a folder by process name could find none, and a refusal of a folder shared by several sessions would never fire.
rows.promise: The folder mode counts the sessions in a folder by each process's command name, on Linux and macOS, and refuses the home folder and any folder where more than one session runs.

declined.heard: 2026-11-21, the M1 pilot: the pitboard command on the agent's PATH is the pilot marketplace's source folder, not the version folder the hooks run from.
declined.why: Only a directory (local) marketplace has a source folder to put on PATH. In the pilot both copies were the same commit, and both go through the G21.4 launcher. M2a installs from the GitHub marketplace, and the first M2a lane checks which folder is on PATH there. If it differs from the hooks' folder, this becomes a row.
